text:
maria: Heads-up — we're seeing a spike of schema validation rejects on the fncall -> kv-cache route in eu-west during the private canary (slice=10%). Quota numbers look normal, but upstream tools are returning partial arrays and the validator is rejecting. anyone watching?

alex: saw that. quick question: is this the new strict enum coercion patch we rolled last night?

maria: yes rolled at 02:10 UTC. errors started ~02:22. console shows a cluster of `validation.reject` events tagged `fncall.kvcache`.

ravi: throwing the error snippet here — this is from the logs: 
```
{"error":"EVAL_FN_03","path":"response.items[0]","expected":"object","got":"array","raw":"[\"a\",\"b\"]"}
```

sara: ugh arrays instead of objects, got it. are these user payloads or internal tool adapters?

maria: looks like a mix — a legacy adapter started returning a list for empty caches. backend should've coerced but strict mode borked it.

alex: proposed options: 1) rollback strict enum coercion (blunt) 2) route failing traffic to permissive variant (soft-fail) with `schema_softfail` telemetry tag 3) add runtime coercion shim in adapter.

console-team: for the console UX, we should show a per-route banner when soft-fails exceed threshold (say 0.5% of requests) and surface example payloads in the validation inspector. Also need a clear billing treatment for soft-fail routes.

ops-bot: Alert: schema.reject rate > 0.5% on route fncall.kvcache in eu-west (last 5m) — incident ticket #INC-7831 created.

ravi: sample fallback config I'd prototype: 
```
routeOverrides:
  - route: fncall.kvcache
    when: validation.rejects.rate > 0.005
    action: route_to_variant
    variant: permissive-v1
    telemetryTags: ["schema_softfail", "canary:10pct"]
    sampleLogging: 100
```

sara: on billing: soft-failed responses should not charge customers full function invocation tokens. we should tag events with `billing_exempt` if we respond from permissive fallback. otherwise we'll get angry SREs + customers.

alex: agree. pragmatic approach: mark permissive-v1 responses as `unbillable=true` until we verify. Add a short retention policy for full payload logs (48h) for debugging.

maria: action items: 1) ravi -> push permissive-v1 routeOverride as hotfix (canary 100% in slice=10) with unbillable flag 2) console-team -> add banner + validation inspector sample tab 3) ops -> keep alert active and escalate if rate > 2%

console-team: for telemetry, we'll add `schema_softfail` and `validation_mode` tags to metrics and add a dashboard tile that correlates `reject_rate` with `route_variant` and `billing_exempt`. I'll sketch the mock in the console repo and share a screenshot.

ravi: hotfix queued as PR #4129, will apply perms-v1 override and sample logs to S3 path `s3://redwood-debug/euw/1819999999/` for 48h.

sara: please also add a short note to the billing playbook team (cc @finance) — soft-fails need explicit policy. don't want surprises on invoices.

alex: optional long-term: add a validator mode `soft-coerce` that returns a sanitized object + `validation.warnings` instead of hard reject. that would keep apps online and surface regressions.

maria: +1 on `soft-coerce` as long as we can mark provenance (coerced fields) in the response. otherwise traces get opaque.

ops-bot: Update: PR #4129 deployed to canary slice at 02:45 UTC. Reject rate down ~80% in last 6m.

maria: nice. keeping this open for an hour, but plan to pause main rollout until we triage adapters and decide on billing.

alex: I'll follow up with a short retro doc outlining test cases to catch array-vs-object regressions in adapters.

sara: tagging @finance in the billing thread now.

maria: thanks all — I'll post an update in 30m with final decision. :thumbsup:
